title: Emergency SLO Attenuator and Rolling Fallback Safety Net
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces an emergency SLO attenuator (ambulance mode) to allow controlled temporary relaxation of non-critical SLOs and an automated rolling fallback safety net that performs staggered model/region fallback with strong telemetry and audit logs. Backward-compatible toggle; safe by default.
description:
Context: We observed two incidents in the last month where large regional maintenance windows caused SLO enforcement to aggressively circuit dozens of tenant requests simultaneously, producing cascading failovers and elevated error rates in downstream systems. This PR introduces an "ambulance mode" SLO attenuator + rolling fallback safety net to reduce cascade risk during emergency conditions.

Goals:
1) Provide a fast, auditable emergency toggle for SRE to relax non-critical SLO enforcement thresholds for a short window.
2) Ensure fallbacks are applied in a rolling, paced manner across nodes/regions to avoid synchronized re-routing spikes.
3) Emit clear telemetry and audit events so post-incident analysis can attribute decisions and quantify residual impact.

Summary of changes:
- runtime/serving/attenuator.go: new Attenuator service that evaluates per-tenant SLO attenuation policies and exposes a lightweight API for the control plane to request temporary attenuation. Includes an in-memory short-lived lease mechanism and a conservative decay timer to avoid rapid flip-flopping.
- controlplane/handlers/slo_attenuator.go: control plane endpoint which SRE and the console can call to enable/disable ambulance mode; validates RBAC and writes audit entries to the existing audit log.
- orchestrator/fallback/rolling_fallback.go: implements rolling fallback orchestration: when a fallback is required the coordinator assigns phased fallback windows to nodes and tracks progress to minimize instantaneous load shifts.
- console/api/v1/attenuator_toggle.go and console/ui/alerts: UI and API enablement for operators; toggles show a clear TTL, scope (tenant/global/region), and a link to the suppressible alert rule.
- telemetry/metrics/attenuator_metrics.prom and telemetry/events/attacks_audit.log: new metrics and structured audit events for attenuation actions, fallback phases, and rollback triggers.
- tests/integration/attenuator_e2e_test.go: canary-style integration test that simulates a regional maintenance and asserts that fallbacks are rolled out without >10% spike in QPS to any single target.
- docs/ops/ambulance-mode.md: runbook describing when to enable, guardrails, and postmortem steps.

Rollout and safety:
- Feature gated behind a cluster feature flag (default: disabled).
- Must be enabled via Console or CLI and requires an approval step in Linear for production clusters.
- Default attenuation only relaxes non-critical SLO buckets (e.g., best-effort token deadlines/latency SLOs) and never disables critical correctness/authorization checks.
- All attenuation actions create audit events and a linked Linear ticket suggestion for follow-up.

CI: unit tests and linters run on initial push; integration e2e initially failed intermittently in CI (flaky timing in the test harness), fixed by adding a more deterministic clock stub and retry backoff in the test. See commit history for fixes.

Checklist:
- [x] Attenuator runtime implementation
- [x] Control plane toggle + RBAC
- [x] Rolling fallback coordinator
- [x] Telemetry + audit events
- [x] Integration tests and runbook
- [x] Safety feature flag and TTL guard

Related: Builds on prior work for staged failover orchestration (ENG-0821) and ties into the SRE incident responder flows (SRE-210).
